analysis:
TSM fell 10.2%, 5.7 points more than the market's 4.4% decline, and tracked closely with its AI compute peers, which saw a median drop of 10.3%. The coverage collectively points to a broad semiconductor selloff, with headlines noting TSMC's decline alongside Nvidia's $1.4 trillion loss since October, a chip rout deepening after Democratic midterm wins, and comparisons between chipmakers during the AI selloff. One piece notes TSMC fell despite a $53.3 billion revenue midpoint, while others discuss AMD versus TSMC and investment choices among chip stocks, though these are headlines only without article detail.

The stock has shown unusual behavior around earnings, with five of the last seven reports delivering estimate beats followed by negative moves beyond the market -- most recently a 1.7% beat in October that brought a -2.5 percentage point abnormal decline. The typical move around earnings beyond what the market explains is 2.5 percentage points, meaning beating estimates has not reliably translated into gains. The company reports next on January 14, 70 days out.
